title: Promise, prediction, description, and commendation
summary: The content and context of an assurance determine whether it commits the speaker to a result.
notes: Hawkins distinguishes an asserted guarantee from estimates of recovery time. Bayliner distinguishes a performance description of another configuration and general promotional praise from a warranty about the goods sold. A statement’s specificity, its relation to the actual subject, and its place in the transaction matter. A disappointing outcome alone does not establish a promise. The textbook’s theories of promise then ask why a sufficiently identified assurance should receive legal enforcement.
